COMMERCIAL LOBBY DESIGN
07

label: Page 9
text:
The commercial stilt lobby forms the primary arrival and transition space of the building, 
creating a refined threshold between the street and the workplace. Designed as a welcoming, 
contemporary environment, the lobby integrates reception, lift access, waiting areas, wayfinding, 
and landscaped pockets within a cohesive material palette. Stone surfaces, warm wood detailing, 
glass partitions, integrated lighting, and built-in seating create a sophisticated yet comfortable 
atmosphere, while carefully planned circulation ensures an intuitive movement through the space. 
The lobby establishes a strong first impression while balancing functionality, identity, and everyday 
user experience.

THE FOLD HOUSE
15

label: Page 17
text:
The Fold House is envisioned as a contemporary family retreat in Alibaug, designed to offer a 
peaceful escape from the pace of urban life while encouraging a deeper connection with nature. 
The design explores the reinterpretation of traditional pitched-roof architecture through a series of 
folded planes, clean geometric volumes, and carefully framed openings. Its distinctive roof form 
defines the architectural identity while creating opportunities for natural light, ventilation, and 
spatial interaction. The residence balances openness and privacy through thoughtfully arranged 
living spaces, allowing a small family to experience comfort, functionality, and togetherness. Rooted 
in simplicity and responsive to Alibaug's tropical coastal climate, The Fold House seeks to create a 
timeless living environment where contemporary architecture meets the warmth of a family home.

Furniture Design / Rhino + Grasshopper
PARAMETRIC BENCH
25

label: Page 27
text:
This project explores the relationship between computational design, material efficiency, and 
fabrication. Developed in Rhino and Grasshopper, the bench is generated through a parametric 
system that transforms a basic volume into a fluid, sculptural form.
The design is controlled through adjustable parameters including height, width, curvature, and 
section spacing. The resulting form is then divided into a series of structural profiles, which are 
organized and nested for efficient fabrication. This workflow demonstrates how Grasshopper can 
connect design exploration with rationalized production, allowing multiple variations to be tested 
while maintaining a clear and adaptable design logic.

MASTER BATH
33

label: Page 35
text:
The master bathroom is designed as a refined and functional private retreat, balancing clean 
contemporary detailing with a warm, natural material palette. The layout separates the wet and 
dry zones, with a spacious walk-in shower featuring recessed storage niches, integrated seating, 
and coordinated fixtures. A wall-mounted WC maintains visual openness, while the custom timber 
vanity provides generous storage and a practical wash area. Soft ambient lighting, warm wood 
finishes, neutral wall surfaces, and carefully integrated accessories create a calm, comfortable, 
and cohesive bathroom environment.

Parametric Design / Rhino + Grasshopper
FACADE DESIGN
38

label: Page 40
text:
The facade is conceived as a layered architectural screen that balances enclosure, daylight, 
and visual permeability. A triangular grid establishes its underlying order, while an attractor 
curve introduces local variation: panels shift in scale and depth according to their relationship 
with the curve. This creates a gradual transition across the elevation rather than a uniform, 
repetitive surface.
The changing panel geometry gives the facade depth and shadow, bringing its pattern to 
life as light conditions shift. From an architectural perspective, the attractor acts as a design 
driver—not merely a visual effect—organising variation across the elevation while maintaining a
coherent modular system. The result is a facade that combines geometric discipline with a more 
responsive, expressive character.
39

label: Page 41
text:
Parametric Design / Rhino + Grasshopper
01  /  Set the facade boundary
A rectangular surface defines the overall 
size and limits of the facade.
02  /  Create the triangular grid
The surface is divided into a regular field of 
triangular cells, establishing the screen’s 
base pattern.
03  /  Locate each cell center
The center point of each triangle is 
calculated so the cells can respond 
individually to the design logic.
FACADE DESIGN
30
30
04  /  Introduce the attractor curve
An attractor curve is placed near the grid. 
The distance from each cell center to the 
curve determines how strongly that cell is 
affected.
05  / Vary the triangular openings
The remapped values scale the triangular 
geometry, creating a perforation pattern
that changes in size across the screen 
while retaining the underlying grid.
06  /  Construct the facade panels
The resulting curves define the panel regions 
and their openings, forming a continuous, 
patterned metal screen.
